title: Garage Workshop Remodel & French Cleat Tool Wall
excerpt: A full workshop remodel with a more efficient layout and a versatile French cleat wall system for tool organization.
body:
## Overview
Over the past few months, I’ve been remodeling my workshop to improve both layout and functionality.

The available space was limited to a section of my garage measuring approximately 7m by 4m, so maximizing efficiency and organization was essential.

## Layout Planning
The first step of the remodel was rethinking the overall layout.

The goal was to create a workflow that allows smooth transitions between cutting, assembly and finishing areas, while keeping tools accessible and organized.

## French Cleat System
One of the biggest upgrades in this project was building a French cleat tool wall system.

A French cleat system consists of wooden strips cut at a 45-degree angle. One strip is mounted to the wall, and matching pieces are attached to tool holders.

This creates a strong and flexible mounting system that allows tools and accessories to be easily repositioned.

## Advantages of French Cleats
- Fully modular and adjustable
- Strong load capacity
- Keeps tools visible and accessible
- Easy to expand over time

This system is ideal for workshops because it adapts as your tool collection grows.

## Build Process
The process involved installing horizontal cleats across the wall and then creating custom holders for different tools.

Each holder can be moved or replaced at any time without damaging the wall, making the system extremely versatile.

## Final Result
With the new layout and the French cleat system in place, the workshop became much more organized and efficient.

This upgrade allows better use of available space while improving productivity and workflow.
